mainProgression.description: Simple but deeply funky two-chord vamp that drives the entire song, creating tension between minor tonic and dominant seventh

sectionProgressions.romanNumerals: bVI - III - bVI - III - i - V7
sectionProgressions.description: Introduces contrasting chords before returning to the main vamp, adding harmonic variety

harmonicFunction: Ebm (i) - Tonic minor chord providing the dark, funky foundation
Bb7 (V7) - Dominant seventh creating forward motion and tension that resolves back to Ebm
B (bVI) - Flat sixth chord in the bridge providing harmonic contrast
Gb (III) - Mediant chord adding modal brightness in bridge sections

techniques.name: Funk Rhythm Guitar
techniques.description: Staccato funk strumming pattern adapted from the iconic clavinet riff, featuring muted strings, syncopated accents, and tight 16th-note rhythmic feel

notes: The clavinet riff translates to guitar as a single-note line on the low strings: Eb-Gb-Ab-Bb pattern
Use heavy palm muting between notes for staccato articulation
Muted string scratches (ghost notes) fill the gaps between pitched notes
Keep the picking hand moving in constant 16th-note motion for consistent groove
Accent placement on the and-of-beat-two and beat-four drives the funk feel
Fretting hand lifts slightly for muted scratches without fully releasing the strings
sequence: Establish constant 16th-note picking motion with the right hand
Play the note at the correct fret position with a sharp staccato attack
Follow with muted ghost strums to maintain the 16th-note pulse
Play the note at the correct fret position, then Ab on the 11th fret with same staccato approach
Complete the phrase with Bb on the 1st fret of the D string
Return to the Eb and repeat the pattern with variations in accent placement
tips: Practice the muted strum technique separately before adding pitched notes
Use a metronome at 80 BPM and gradually work up to 100 BPM
Keep your wrist loose and relaxed for fluid 16th-note motion
Listen to the original clavinet part closely to internalize the rhythmic feel
Record yourself and compare accents to the original groove

techniques.name: Wah-Wah Pedal Technique
techniques.description: Using the wah pedal to emulate the vowel-like tonal shifts of the original clavinet, adding expressive filter sweeps to rhythm and lead playing

notes: Rock the wah pedal in sync with the rhythmic accents of the riff
Toe-down position emphasizes treble for sharp, cutting accents
Heel-down position warms the tone for background texture
Half-cocked (partially open) wah position creates a nasally, clavinet-like tone
Coordinate foot movement with picking hand for musical expression
sequence: Start with heel-down position during muted ghost strums
Rock to toe-down on accented notes for a sharp, bright punch
Return to heel-down between accents for rhythmic contrast
Experiment with half-cocked positions during sustained notes
Combine wah sweeps with volume dynamics for deeper expression
tips: Practice wah control without guitar first to build foot coordination
Sync the wah sweep to quarter notes initially, then try 8th notes
A half-cocked wah position can approximate the clavinet's nasal tone
Don't overuse the wah - let some phrases play clean for contrast
Try a slow sweep during held notes for a vocal quality

sections.name: Intro
sections.description: The iconic clavinet riff opens the song, adapted for guitar as a single-note funk line on the lower strings with staccato articulation and syncopated timing
notes: The riff is the signature hook - nail the staccato feel
Keep ghost notes between pitched notes for consistent groove
Start with the drums-only intro feel, then lock in with the bass
Use bridge pickup and slight wah for an authentic tone

sections.name: Verse
sections.description: The verse maintains the two-chord Ebm-Bb7 vamp underneath the vocals, with the guitar providing rhythmic comping and occasional single-note fills
notes: Pull back the intensity slightly to leave room for vocals
Use muted strums more heavily during vocal phrases
Accent the chord changes to mark the harmonic rhythm
Keep the wah subtle during verses to avoid competing with the voice

sections.name: Chorus
sections.description: The chorus builds intensity with the same chord progression but more aggressive rhythmic accents and fuller strumming
notes: Increase strumming intensity for the chorus lift
Play fuller chord voicings rather than single notes
Add more aggressive wah pedal movement for energy
Emphasize the downbeat resolution back to Ebm

sections.name: Bridge
sections.description: The bridge introduces the B and Gb chords for harmonic contrast, shifting away from the Ebm-Bb7 vamp before returning to it
sections.progression: B - Gb - B - Gb - Ebm - Bb7
notes: The chord change to B and Gb provides a welcome contrast
Use barre chord voicings for the B chord with clean strumming
Transition smoothly back to the Ebm vamp after the bridge
Build rhythmic intensity through the bridge to set up the return

sections.name: Outro
sections.description: The song rides out on the main riff with increasing intensity, improvisational fills, and a fade-out that keeps the groove locked in
notes: Add improvisational variations to the main riff
Increase wah pedal activity for excitement
Maintain tight rhythmic feel even as intensity increases
The groove must stay locked even during ad-lib sections

guitar.pickup: Bridge single-coil pickup for bright, cutting funk tone with clear note definition

effects.distortion: None to very slight overdrive - keep the tone clean and punchy
effects.reverb: Minimal spring reverb for subtle ambience
effects.other: Wah pedal (Dunlop Cry Baby or Vox V847) is essential for the clavinet-inspired tone; optional auto-wah/envelope filter for more authentic clavinet emulation

beginner.focus: Learn the basic single-note riff pattern and Ebm chord shape
steps: Learn the Eb minor pentatonic scale in the 6th position on the A string
Practice the four-note riff pattern (Eb-Gb-Ab-Bb) slowly without syncopation
Master the Ebm and Bb7 chord shapes for the basic progression
Practice strumming the Ebm-Bb7 vamp at a slow tempo with a metronome

intermediate.focus: Develop the funk rhythm feel with ghost notes, staccato, and wah pedal integration
steps: Add ghost notes (muted strums) between pitched notes in the riff
Practice the 16th-note strumming pattern with syncopated accents
Introduce the wah pedal and practice coordinating foot and hand movement
Learn all song sections including the bridge chord changes (B and Gb)

advanced.focus: Master the complete performance with improvisational fills and authentic funk feel
steps: Perfect the tight staccato funk feel at full tempo (100 BPM)
Add improvisational pentatonic fills over the verse sections
Master wah pedal expression with varied sweep speeds and positions
Perform the entire song with dynamics, building from verse to chorus to outro

commonMistakes: Playing notes too long - staccato articulation is essential for the funk feel
Neglecting ghost notes between pitched notes, which kills the groove
Overusing the wah pedal instead of using it musically and rhythmically
Playing the riff with too much gain or distortion, losing the clean punch
practiceRoutine: Warm up with Eb minor pentatonic scale runs at moderate tempo for 5 minutes
Practice the four-note riff pattern slowly focusing on staccato articulation
Work on 16th-note ghost note strumming at 80 BPM for 10 minutes
Combine pitched notes and ghost notes at gradually increasing tempos
Run through full song sections with a backing track
focusAreas: 16th-note rhythmic consistency and ghost note placement
Wah pedal coordination with picking hand rhythm
Clean funk tone with tight low-end control
metronomeWork: Start at 70 BPM with straight 16th-note ghost strums only
Add pitched notes at 80 BPM while maintaining the ghost note pulse
Increase to 90 BPM focusing on syncopated accent placement
Reach target tempo of 100 BPM with full groove and dynamics
